newsitem.title: UK: UK's Galen trumpets track record ahead of listing.
newsitem.headline: UK's Galen trumpets track record ahead of listing.

text.p: Northern Ireland-based pharmaceutical company Galen Holdings Plc, which plans to float London Stock Exchange in July, said on Wednesday it should not be compared to other biotechnology companies.
In an interview with Reuters, chief executive John King pointed to the company's record of 29 years of profitable growth through established products and services.
"The point to underline is we are different," said King. "We have a vertical structure through R&D, manufacturing and marketing."
The company is expected to raise 30 million stg from the float and have a market capitalisation of 180 million stg. Dealings are predicted to start on July 10.
Galen, one of the largest manufacturers in Northern Ireland, employing around 600 people, said it would use the proceeds to expand and develop its existing businesses and fund acquisitions.

Its ethical pharmaceutical products business, which accounts for 75 percent of turnover, includes the manufacture and marketing of prescription medicines which are sold in the UK and Ireland via a sales force of about 50 representatives.

The pharmaceutical products business also involves the research and development of new ways of delivering drugs, notably an intravaginal ring (IVR) which can release one or more drugs at a prescribed rate inside a patient.
Galen's hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is being developed with the use of IVR and is in clinical phase 3 of testing.

The company's other main business - ethical pharmaceutical services - provides clinical trial services to other pharmaceutical companies who wish to outsource the manufacture, packaging and distribution of drugs to clinical trial patients.
Galen's pharmaceutical services customers include Glaxo Wellcome Plc, Janssen, Pfizer Inc and Zeneca Group Plc.

The company made pre-tax profits for the year to September 30 1996 of 7.2 million stg against 3.6 million for the previous year. Turnover was 31.1 million stg in the fiscal year 1996 compared to 23.3 million in 1995.
In the current year, Galen said in the six months to March 31 it made pre-tax profits of 5.4 million.
Finance director Geoffrey Elliott said Galen remained a growth company but would pay a dividend which would probably be under one percent annual gross yield.
Galen also announced the proposed formation of two new trusts through the donation of 11 percent of existing ordinary shares by the founder and chairman Allen McClay.

One trust, which is intended to have charitable status, will be to fund research by the Schools of Chemistry and Pharmacy at the Queen's University of Belfast - an established source for Galen employees.
Another trust is being created for employees who have worked for the company for over five years.
